speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a history of AIDS and are experiencing vision loss with floaters in your right eye. To narrow down the cause, have you noticed any pain when moving your eyes or any flashes of light?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Given your past Kaposi's sarcoma and recent fungal infection, have you noticed any new skin lesions or oral ulcers, and does the vision change occur with movement? REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy. REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Eye_Fundus.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis.

The findings of granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages in your right eye are classic for CMV retinitis, a common opportunistic infection in patients with advanced HIV/AIDS. Given your history of AIDS and the specific appearance of the retinal damage, this is the most likely cause of your vision loss.
